name: PCF8574 8-bit I/O expander
description: TI/NXP 8-bit quasi-bidirectional I/O expander for I2C (100 kHz): one written byte sets P7..P0, one read byte returns their levels; no direction register. A pin latched high is a weak 30-310 uA pull-up that can be read as an input; latched low it sinks up to 25 mA (100 mA total), so drive LEDs active-low from VCC. Chip supply 2.5-6 V, I2C address 0x20-0x27 (0100 A2 A1 A0). Sold as: Adafruit PCF8574 I2C GPIO Expander Breakout (#5545), two headers modelled as one 16-pin row: power/I2C row VIN, GND, SCL, SDA, INT, A0, then I/O row +, P7, P6, P5, P4, P3, P2, P1, P0, -; STEMMA QT connectors; address 0x20 with A0 and the A1/A2 jumpers open.
eli5: Gives your board eight extra on/off pins over just two I2C wires, for buttons and LEDs.

pins.description: Supply, 3-5 V: use the same voltage as your microcontroller's logic (chip: 2.5-6 V)

pins.description: I2C clock (10 k pull-up on the board), 100 kHz max

pins.name: INT
pins.description: Interrupt output, open-drain, active low: goes low when an input pin changes; cleared by reading or writing the port

pins.description: Address bit 0: unconnected = 0x20, tie to VIN = 0x21 (A1/A2 are solder jumpers on the back)

supplierQuery: Adafruit PCF8574 I2C GPIO expander breakout 5545
buildNotes: Run the I2C bus at 100 kHz (I2C(..., freq=100000)): the PCF8574 is a standard-mode part and 400 kHz is out of spec.
There are no registers: write one byte to set all eight pins, read one byte to get all eight levels (bit 7 = P7).
A pin can only pull high weakly (about 100 uA). Wire LEDs from + through a resistor (e.g. 1 k) into the P pin so they light when the pin is written 0.
To use a pin as an input, write it 1 first (all pins are 1 at power-on), then wire the button from the pin to GND: pressed reads 0.
Address 0x20 by default; tie A0 to VIN or close the A0/A1/A2 jumpers on the back for 0x21-0x27 (up to 8 boards on one bus).
Never short a pin that is written 0 to VIN: it sinks up to 25 mA per pin and 100 mA in total.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from pcf8574 import PCF8574

# The PCF8574 is a 100 kHz (standard-mode) I2C device.
i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}), freq=100000)
io = PCF8574(i2c, 0x20)
# Button from P7 to GND; LED + 1 k resistor from + to P0 (lights when P0 is pulled low).
while True:
    pressed = io.pin(7) == 0      # P7 stays latched high, so it reads the button
    io.pin(0, 0 if pressed else 1)
    print('BUTTON=%s LED=%s' % ('PRESSED' if pressed else 'RELEASED', 'ON' if pressed else 'OFF'))
    time.sleep_ms(200)

test.title: Reads the button on P7 and sinks P0 low to light the LED
